title: Forgiveness in Marriage
author: Justin Myko Agpangan
summary: A brief devotional essay arguing that forgiveness is structurally necessary to Christian marriage because marriage joins two justified-but-still-sinning people, not two perfected ones. The author grounds the claim theologically: believers are new creations indwelt by the Spirit yet still contend with remaining sin, so spouses will inevitably hurt and disappoint one another this side of glorification. Because Christians have already received costly forgiveness through Christ's atoning death, the argument runs, they are both obligated and equipped to extend that same forgiveness to a spouse rather than expect sinlessness from them. The author is careful to distinguish forgiveness from permissiveness: pursuing holiness and mutual fidelity remain binding obligations, and forgiveness is never license to keep sinning against one's spouse. The practical upshot is a call to renounce pride, confess quickly, and forgive readily, framed explicitly as a public witness to the gospel's power.
points: Roots marital forgiveness in ongoing sanctification: because spouses remain simultaneously justified and still sinning, friction and hurt in marriage are expected rather than exceptional.
Distinguishes forgiveness from tolerance of continued sin, insisting mutual fidelity and pursuit of holiness remain binding even as grace is extended.
Frames each spouse's forgiveness of the other as flowing directly from, and modeled on, the forgiveness already received through Christ's atonement.
Positions a forgiving marriage as public testimony, arguing that reconciliation between spouses displays the gospel's power to outside observers.
quotes: Forgiveness is important in marriage because marriage does not make us sinless. Marriage is a joining of two sinners who are in need of God's forgiveness in the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ.

So we should never expect perfection from our spouses. We are far from perfect. Even though we are radically different from who we were when we were still unbelievers, we are still undergoing the process of being transformed to the image of Jesus.
In light of that, forgiveness is essential in marriage. Forgiving others are rooted to the gift of forgiveness that we have received through faith in Jesus.

We owe God big time because of our sins. Jesus paid our great debt by His life and by His death. In light of that, we can forgive our spouses because our many and our great sins have already been forgiven by God through Jesus.
Forgiveness makes marriages work as designed by God. Bitterness and anger towards are spouses destroy marriages. Through forgiveness, we put off destructive emotions and put on compassion and love.
